full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 234

Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Co., Ltd. v. (Application for Establishment of a Fund for Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims)

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on November 25, 2024)

Keywords
Civil; application for establishment of a fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims; amount of fund; ocean-going vessel; coastal vessel

Ruling Gist
Where, in the same maritime accident, the limitation amount for a vessel involved in the accident should be calculated in accordance with Article 210, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China or Article 3 of the Provisions on the Limitation Amount for Maritime Claims of Ships of Less than 300 Gross Tonnage and for Coastal Transport and Coastal Operations, regardless of whether such vessel has applied to establish a fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims or has asserted the right to limit liability, the limitation amount for other vessels involved in the same accident shall not be subject to Article 4 of the said Provisions.

Basic Facts
The vessel "Hua Mou Zhou," owned by Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Company"), was a seagoing ship of 2,986 gross tonnage engaged in domestic coastal and middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River general cargo transportation. On November 21, 2020, the "Hua Mou Zhou" collided with the Singapore-flagged vessel "Mou Chun" (27,800 gross tonnage), owned by Wan Mou Shipping (Singapore) Co., Ltd., near Anchorage No. 32 in the Pearl River Estuary, causing partial damage to both vessels and partial loss of containers and cargo on board the "Mou Chun."

On December 28, 2020, Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Company applied to the Guangzhou Maritime Court for the establishment of a fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims in the amount of 291,081 Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) (calculated at 50% of the limitation amount) in respect of all non-personal injury liabilities that might arise from the collision between the "Hua Mou Zhou" and the "Mou Chun," pursuant to Article 4 of the Provisions on the Limitation Amount for Maritime Claims of Ships of Less than 300 Gross Tonnage and for Coastal Transport and Coastal Operations (hereinafter "Provisions on Limitation Amount"). Wan Mou Shipping (Singapore) Co., Ltd. did not apply for the establishment of a fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims.

The Guangzhou Maritime Safety Administration and Wan Mou Shipping (Singapore) Co., Ltd. raised no objection to Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Company's legal standing or to the nature of the claims involved in the accident, but objected to the amount of the fund for limitation of liability. They contended that one of the vessels involved in the accident, the "Mou Chun," was a Singapore-flagged vessel, and its voyage was from Singapore to Nansha Port, Guangzhou, China. Therefore, under Article 5 of the Provisions on Limitation Amount, the "Hua Mou Zhou" should calculate the amount of the fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims in accordance with the standard set forth in Article 210, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code, and could not apply the 50% calculation provided for in Article 4 of the Provisions on Limitation Amount. Accordingly, the limitation amount for the fund applied for by Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Company should be set at 582,162 SDRs plus corresponding interest.

Judgment
The Guangzhou Maritime Court rendered a civil ruling on April 2, 2021 [(2021) Yue 72 Min Te No. 5]:
1. The application of Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Co., Ltd. for the establishment of a fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims was granted;
2. The amount of the fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims was set at 582,162 SDRs plus interest;
3. The applicant, Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Co., Ltd., was ordered to establish the fund in RMB or security acceptable to the court within three days from the effective date of this ruling. Failure to establish the fund within the time limit would be deemed as automatic withdrawal of the application.
No party appealed the ruling, which has become legally effective.

Reasoning
This case involves an application for the establishment of a fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims. The disputed issue is whether the amount of the fund for the "Hua Mou Zhou" should be calculated at 50% of the limitation amount provided for in Article 210, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code.

The limitation amount for maritime claims is the maximum amount of compensation that a liable party is legally obligated to pay for all limitable claims, including personal injury claims and non-personal injury claims. Article 210, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code sets forth specific rules for calculating the limitation amount for ocean-going vessels of 300 gross tonnage or more, applying different standards based on tonnage. On this basis, Article 210, paragraph 2 of the Maritime Code provides: "The limitation amount for ships of less than 300 gross tonnage and for ships engaged in transport between ports of the People's Republic of China, as well as for ships engaged in coastal operations, shall be formulated by the competent authority of transport under the State Council and implemented upon approval by the State Council." Accordingly, with the approval of the State Council, the former Ministry of Transport issued the Provisions on Limitation Amount in November 1993, specifying the calculation standards for the limitation amount for ocean-going vessels of less than 300 gross tonnage. Article 4 of the Provisions establishes a special rule that the limitation amount for ships engaged in coastal cargo transport between ports of the People's Republic of China or coastal operations shall be calculated at 50% of the limitation amount for ocean-going vessels. Furthermore, for the same accident involving both ocean-going vessels and coastal transport or operation vessels, Article 5 of the Provisions on Limitation Amount states: "Where the limitation amount for a vessel involved in the same accident is calculated in accordance with Article 210 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China or Article 3 of these Provisions, the limitation amount for other vessels involved in the same accident shall likewise apply." This Article effectively establishes a "higher of the applicable limits" rule, aiming to ensure equal protection for parties involved in the same accident. Accordingly, as long as any vessel involved in the same accident is a vessel whose limitation amount is calculated under Article 210, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code or Article 3 of the Provisions on Limitation Amount — regardless of whether that vessel has applied to establish a fund for limitation of liability or asserted the right to limit liability — other vessels involved in the accident that are engaged in cargo transport between ports of the People's Republic of China or coastal operations must also calculate their limitation amounts using the same rules based on their tonnage, and can no longer apply the 50% calculation provided for in Article 4 of the Provisions on Limitation Amount.

In this case, the maritime accident involved a collision between the "Hua Mou Zhou" and the "Mou Chun." The "Hua Mou Zhou" was a seagoing vessel engaged in domestic coastal and middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River general cargo transportation. The "Mou Chun" was a Singapore-flagged vessel, and its voyage was from Singapore to Nansha Port, Guangzhou, China. The "Mou Chun" was an ocean-going vessel of more than 300 gross tonnage, which should have its limitation amount determined under Article 210, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code. Regardless of whether the "Mou Chun" applied for the establishment of a fund for limitation of liability or invoked the defense of limitation of liability, the limitation amount for the "Hua Mou Zhou" should be calculated based on its tonnage and could not be calculated at 50% of the limitation amount. Therefore, since the "Hua Mou Zhou" was a vessel of more than 300 gross tonnage, its limitation amount should be subject to Article 210, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code, the same as the "Mou Chun."

In conclusion, the court upheld the objection raised by the Guangzhou Maritime Safety Administration and Wan Mou Shipping (Singapore) Co., Ltd. that Nanjing Hua Mou Shipping Company was not entitled to calculate its limitation amount under Article 4 of the Provisions on Limitation Amount.

Relevant Legal Provisions
Article 210 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China
Articles 3, 4, and 5 of the Provisions on the Limitation Amount for Maritime Claims of Ships of Less than 300 Gross Tonnage and for Coastal Transport and Coastal Operations (Ministry of Transport Order No. 5 of 1993)
